name: Neutral earthing resistor
summary: A resistor between a transformer or generator neutral and earth that limits earth-fault current to a set value.
description: A neutral earthing resistor connects the star point of a transformer or generator to earth through a defined resistance. It limits earth-fault current, typically to tens or hundreds of amperes on medium-voltage systems and a few amperes on high-resistance earthed low-voltage systems, reducing damage and arc energy while keeping enough current for protection to detect.

Drawings show a resistor between the neutral of a star winding and the earth symbol, often with a current transformer in the neutral lead for earth-fault protection and sometimes a disconnector. The resistor current and time rating, such as 400 A for 10 seconds, are written beside it.

The symbol does not show the resistor's monitoring, which some designs use to detect an open resistor. It also does not show whether generator and transformer neutrals are earthed at the same time, which affects fault current and circulating harmonic currents.
readingNotes: Read the current and time rating together.
A neutral CT normally feeds earth-fault protection.
drawingChecklist: State resistance, current and time rating.
distinction: A neutral earthing resistor limits fault current resistively; an arc suppression coil compensates capacitive fault current with inductance.
